items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Roy Eldridge, Lester Young, Ray Brown, Joe Benjamin and Norman Grantz the organiser of the J.A.T.P. came to the cocktail.

ctx.x: I did my second concert in a different theatre from the first one and in a different part of the city. There was a German trumpetist on the bill that night who was known as the best jazz trumpeter in Germany. His name was Macky Kasper and he was good. But his main claim to fame was that he could blow loud. He had some "iron chops" as we say in musical terms for a trumpeter. After the concert I went back to the club I had visited the night before and jammed with the cats again. Tiger Jones was also on the scene.…

In April I did concerts and balls in France and Belgium. The 7th I was coming back when Lily and Jimmy Davis met me at the railroad station. Jimmy told me that he was engaged to do a cabaret scene in a movie being filmed called 'The Respectful Prostitute', from a Jean-Paul Sartre novel. Joe Benjamin, the bass man and Bill Clark a drummer, were in France with Lena Horne, and they were going to make this cabaret scene also. Aaron Bridges was the pianist. The film featured an American Negro Shakesparian actor named…
We did one of Jimmie's tunes called "The blues jumped and got me", and we were only in the studio for two days. The loot was not much but it was fun making the film.
